CORPORATE DISCLOSURE STATEMENT

Per Supreme Court Rule 29.6, Petitioners state that they have no parent com-

pany or publicly held company with a 10% or greater ownership interest in it.

i

Pursuant to Rules 22 and 33.1(d), Appellants/Petitioners (“Appellants”) re-

spectfully request leave to file a brief on the merits in excess of the word limit, not to

exceed 18,000 words, and a reply brief on the merits in excess of the word limit, not

to exceed 10,000 words.

1.

On January 28, 2022, Appellants filed applications for a stay or injunc-

tive relief pending appeal in two cases—John H. Merrill, Alabama Secretary of State,

et al. v. Evan Milligan, et al., No. 21-1086, and John H. Merrill, Alabama Secretary

of State, et al. v. Marcus Caster, et al., No. 21-1087—related to preliminary injunc-

tions that had been entered by districts courts in both cases based on the same evi-

dence.

2.

On February 7, 2022, the Court in Milligan construed the application as

a jurisdictional statement and noted probable jurisdiction. That same day, the Court

in Caster construed the application as a petition for a writ of certiorari before judg-

ment and granted the petition.

3.

On February 22, 2022, the Court consolidated the cases for briefing and

oral argument and set the same question presented for both cases.

4.

In these consolidated cases, Appellants intend to file a single brief on

the merits and a single reply. Consolidation will prevent needless duplication in ad-

dressing the question presented and other issues the cases have in common.

5.

Though both cases result from the same preliminary injunction proceed-

ings, the Milligan Appellees and Caster Respondents have already demonstrated in

their separate stay-stage briefs that their statutory arguments are not identical,

1

emphasizing different arguments and portions of the record. Moreover, the Milligan

Appellees and Caster Respondents—who filed separate complaints and litigated sep-

arate preliminary injunction motions before the district courts, and who are repre-

sented by separate counsel—have indicated that they intend to file separate response

briefs.

6.

To adequately and efficiently address the issues presented in these

cases, Appellants respectfully request leave to file an opening brief not to exceed

18,000 words, and a reply brief not to exceed 10,000 words. Notably, these consoli-

dated briefs would require fewer words than if Appellants filed two separate opening

briefs (26,000 total words) and two separate reply briefs (12,000 total words).

7.

Appellants have conferred with Appellees and Respondents in both

cases, who do not oppose Appellants’ request.
